mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a single month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if tightening cycles do not correlate with negative returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a single month signals a weakening labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business confidence decline.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if sharp rises in UNRATE do not correlate with negative returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations are revised downwards.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances following two consecutive quarters of GDP decline, or if GDP declines do not correlate with negative returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a single month signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investor sentiment improves.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if sharp increases in INDPRO do not correlate with positive returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 5% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a single month, it signals a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business investment increase.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 5% and PAYEMS increases > 200,000 in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the joint condition does not correlate with positive returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP (GDPC1) growth is positive and housing starts (HOUST) increase by more than 10% in a single month, it signals a robust demand environment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as economic optimism grows.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth > 0% and HOUST increases > 10% in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the joint condition does not correlate with positive returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) over two consecutive months signals inflationary pressure, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the Federal Reserve may tighten monetary policy.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances following two consecutive months of CPI increase, or if CPI increases do not correlate with negative returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant decline in retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 2% in a single month signals weakening consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as corporate earnings expectations are revised downwards.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if sharp declines in RSAFS do not correlate with negative returns (p > 0.05).
